takeaway: Ptosis after transthoracic sympathectomy: injury near the 1st thoracic nerve (T1) interrupts sympathetic fibres to the eye, causing Horner's syndrome.

lines.text: A 28-year-old man has an endoscopic transthoracic sympathectomy.
lines.say: A twenty-eight-year-old man has an endoscopic transthoracic sympathectomy.

lines.text: It treats his palmar hyperhidrosis: very sweaty palms.
The surgeon works on the sympathetic chain inside the chest.
After the operation, his eyelid droops. This is ptosis.
The damage happened near the 1st thoracic nerve, at T1.
lines.say: The damage happened near the first thoracic nerve, at T one.

lines.text: Injury here can interrupt the sympathetic fibres that travel to the eye.
That gives Horner's syndrome, with ptosis of the eye.
